description: Composite two-panel figure of hot-rolled Fe-Mn-Al-C duplex microstructures (panel (b) carries the main claim). (a) is an optical micrograph of a Fe-5Mn-6Al-0.4C steel with a 10 µm scale bar and two overlaid annotations with arrows: "α Ferrite formed at hot rolling temperatures" points to the bright blocky white particles, and "α+κ Phases formed at coiling temperatures" points to the grey banded background. A low-magnification inset at the top right annotates the banded structure as a "δ Band" alternating with "γ Phase Band" and carries its own 25 µm scale bar. (b) is a secondary-electron SEM micrograph of a Fe-2Mn-8Al-0.2C steel (10 µm scale bar; Mag = 1.46 K X; EHT = 20.00 kV) in which a central γ (austenite) plate is encased in a shell of finger-like κ-carbide laths — the arrow marked κ points at that shell — with the surrounding α-ferrite matrix labelled α. Together the panels argue that during hot working α-ferrite forms as isolated particles inside the γ band, whereas in the leaner 2Mn-8Al steel austenite is instead surrounded by a κ-carbide shell at the δ/γ interface, i.e. elemental partitioning during rolling controls which transformation product appears.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, of a Fe-5Mn-6Al-0.4C steel; bright blocky white particles (annotated 'α Ferrite formed at hot rolling temperatures') in a grey matrix (annotated 'α+κ Phases formed at coiling temperatures'). Image is somewhat soft/low-resolution but annotations are legible.

Small inset at top right of (a) with a 25 µm scale bar showing an alternating banded structure annotated 'δ Band' and 'γ Phase Band'; fine detail of the bands is not resolvable at the supplied resolution.

Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, Mag = 1.46 K X, EHT = 20.00 kV, of a Fe-2Mn-8Al-0.2C steel: a central γ (austenite) plate surrounded by a shell of finger/lath-like κ-carbide (arrow 'κ'), embedded in an α-ferrite matrix labelled α.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an optical micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar in which the arrow labelled 'α Ferrite formed at hot rolling temperatures' points to bright, blocky white particles.
The second annotation in panel (a), 'α+κ Phases formed at coiling temperatures', points to the grey banded background matrix of the same micrograph.
The inset in the top right of panel (a) has its own 25 µm scale bar and labels the alternating bands 'δ Band' and 'γ Phase Band'.
Panel (b) is a secondary-electron SEM micrograph with scale bar 10 µm and printed instrument conditions Mag = 1.46 K X and EHT = 20.00 kV.
In panel (b) the letter α labels the surrounding matrix, γ labels a central plate, and an arrow marked κ points to the finger/lath-shaped shell surrounding the γ plate.

The caption states that (a) is an optical microstructure showing α-ferrite formed in the γ phase band (the grey areas in the embedded microstructure) during the hot rolling stage in a Fe-5Mn-6Al-0.4C steel.
The caption states that (b) is an SEM micrograph showing κ phase formed along δ/γ boundaries during the hot rolling stage in a Fe-2Mn-8Al-0.2C steel.
The citing text states that during hot working (reheating and hot rolling) partitioning of C, Mn and Al occurs between the δ and γ phases, accompanied by some γ→α transformation.
The citing text states that the α phase can form along δ/γ boundaries or within γ grains along dislocations, as shown in Fig. 19a for a Fe-5Mn-6Al-0.4C steel.

The citing text states that κ-carbides can form even at hot working temperatures at the interface between austenite and δ-ferrite, forming a shell structure surrounding the austenite, as shown in Fig. 19b.

The citing text states that κ-carbide formation at hot working temperatures is favoured for low C and especially low Mn contents, e.g. 6–8% Al, 2–6% Mn and 0.1–0.3% C, and that increasing Mn can avoid coarse κ-carbides in duplex low-density steels.

Both panels show that the transformation product forms as a distinct shell/particle at the boundary between the austenite (γ) and the ferrite matrix, but the two alloys differ in the product: α-ferrite particles in (a) versus κ-carbide shell in (b).

unreadable_items: panel (a) main micrograph: fine microstructural detail is blurred at the supplied resolution; only coarse bright particles and grey bands are distinguishable
panel (a) inset: the δ Band / γ Phase Band boundaries are visible but individual band thicknesses and internal detail are not resolvable
panel (b): faint dark striations within the central γ plate (possibly a sub-boundary or crack-like feature) cannot be identified
